subject: english-literature
title: Comparing Techniques
welcome_lead: Theme is the doorway; technique is the architecture. Learn to compare form, structure and figurative language.
meta_desc: Comparing techniques and form at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have moved from what is said to how it is said — the literary heart of comparison.

concepts.def: Comparing genre and macro-shape (sonnet vs dramatic monologue, novel vs novella).
Comparing the arrangement of parts (linear vs disrupted, framed vs continuous).
Comparing imagery, metaphor and symbol systems across texts.
Comparing diction, syntax and tone — Latinate vs Anglo-Saxon, formal vs colloquial.
Comparing narrators or speakers — reliability, distance, focalisation.
Comparing how each text positions its reader — sympathetic, ironic, distanced.

walkthroughs.body_html:
If text A is a sonnet and text B a dramatic monologue, the form already encodes radically different reader contracts.

Compare what each form allows and forbids before drilling into local features.
Two texts may share an image set (darkness, water, fire) but use them differently. Compare the symbolic charge — water as cleansing here, drowning there.
Compare narrative voice carefully. A first-person confessional and an omniscient third produce different ethical effects even when handling identical content.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a theme and a symbol?
options: A theme is the title of the book.
A theme is an abstract idea or concern the text explores (e.g. mortality); a symbol is a concrete image that stands for something else (e.g. a skull).
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
Themes are just symbols repeated through the book.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
Modernism just means literature written in modern times.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
Experimentation with form (fragmentation, stream of consciousness), focus on subjective interior experience, scepticism toward traditional narrative and absolute truth.
